title: The integral inverse-image/pullback comparison respects composition
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be isomorphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and inverse images $h^{-1},k^{-1},(kh)^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. On each of $Z,W,V$ use the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,-}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_-$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and the category $D^b_c(-,\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For an isomorphism $g\in\{h,k,kh\}$ let $g^{-1}$ act on complexes with the module structure transported through the structure isomorphism $c_{\mathcal O_E}$, let $Lg^*$ be the completed integral pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $\kappa^g_K:g^{-1}K\to Lg^*K$ be the specified comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b). Let $d_{h,k,K}:h^{-1}k^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}(kh)^{-1}K$ be the canonical isomorphism of inverse images, applied termwise; it is linear for the transported module structures. Let $c^E_{h,k,K}:L(kh)^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lk^*K$ be the specified integral pullback-composition isomorphism of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Then for every $N\in D^b_c(V,\mathcal O_E)$ the object $Lk^*N$ lies in $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, and
$$c^E_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^{kh}_N\circ d_{h,k,N}=\kappa^h_{Lk^*N}\circ h^{-1}(\kappa^k_N):h^{-1}k^{-1}N\longrightarrow Lh^*Lk^*N$$
as morphisms of $D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$. This is an equality of the specified derived morphisms, not merely of their reductions modulo $\varpi_E^n$.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: compatibility of the integral base-change identifications with composition; agent-formulated prerequisite (maintainer reader for lem-trf-integral-point-transport-tower-powers, step 9)

proof.text: The hypotheses on the schemes and coefficient sheaves are exactly those in the inverse-image and completed-pullback definitions. In particular, the integral pullback operation carries the constructible category on $V$ into that on $W$, so $Lk^*N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$. The canonical pseudofunctorial isomorphism of inverse-image functors gives $d_{h,k,N}$; transporting module actions through the structure isomorphisms makes it $\mathcal O_E$-linear. The compatibility of the canonical coefficient maps with inverse-image composition is the ring-sheaf identity of [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition], and the same underlying inverse-image map is applied termwise to $N$.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: compatibility of the integral base-change identifications with composition

proof.text: At a finite coefficient level $A_{E,n}$ choose one flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $N$ and use its quotient complex. By the finite part of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], each $\kappa^g_N$ is represented termwise by the unit map $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], $c_{h,k,N}$ is represented on the same complex by $(kh)^*P\cong h^*k^*P$. Both composites therefore send a local section $x$ to the same tensor $x\otimes1\otimes1$, with the same transported coefficient action; $d_{h,k,N}$ supplies the common source identification. The equality is compatible with all quotient transition maps.

source.place: Definition 18.13.1, Tag 03D6, unit map for module pullback; combined with the termwise composition map of the cited pro-etale pullback lemma

proof.text: For integral coefficients and $g\in\{k,kh\}$ let $P$ be the chosen flat-term K-flat representative of $N$ and let $C_{g,\bullet}$, $C_{g,m}=\operatorname{Res}_mg^*(P_m)$, be the strict reduction tower of the integral comparison definition. Its maps $\theta_{g,m}:g^{-1}P\to C_{g,m}$, $x\mapsto\bar x\otimes1$, satisfy $t_m\circ\theta_{g,m+1}=\theta_{g,m}$, so they define a strict tower map $\theta_g^\Delta:\Delta g^{-1}P\to C_{g,\bullet}$. By [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison] (b), $\kappa^g_N=[\tilde\theta_g]\circ[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}$ with $\tilde\theta_g(z)=(0,(\theta_{g,m}(z))_m)$ landing in the complex $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ of $C_{g,\bullet}$. Countable products of module sheaves on the pro-etale site are exact [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], so the normalized Roos comparison $\rho_{C_g}$ of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] (the class of $\operatorname{Cone}(q_C)$ for a K-injective tower resolution $q_C:C_{g,\bullet}\to I_\bullet$ followed by the inverse of the inclusion $\lim I_\bullet\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1](I_\bullet)$) identifies this cone complex with $R\lim C_{g,\bullet}$; this is the identification under which the counit $\epsilon_{C_g}$ is applied. Under it, $[\tilde\theta_g]$ is the morphism $r_{\theta_g}$ of [lem-trf-integral-cone-counit-realization], whose counit identity gives $\epsilon_{C_g}\circ\Delta(r_{\theta_g})=\theta_g^\Delta$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,-})))$. Hence $\epsilon_{C_g}\circ\Delta(\kappa^g_N)=\theta_g^\Delta\circ\Delta[g^{-1}(q)]^{-1}$: the cone map realizes exactly the compatible family of finite unit maps, before applying any quotient functor or using reduction detection.

source.place: Step 1, Global powers: compatibility of the integral base-change identifications with composition before rationalization

proof.text: Let $M=Lk^*N=R\lim C_{k,\bullet}$ and $D_\bullet=h^*C_{k,\bullet}$; by the defining formula of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], $D_m=h^*k^*P_m=Q_{h,k,E}(P)_m$ and $\eta_{h,k,N}:Lh^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim D_\bullet$. Write $X=h^{-1}k^{-1}N$, represented by $h^{-1}k^{-1}P$. On $Z$, the constant-tower functor $\Delta:\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Z})\to\operatorname{Tow}$ is exact and left adjoint to $\lim$, and the tower category is abelian [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] with K-injective tower resolutions computing $R\lim$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Applying [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] with $G=\Delta$ ($L\Delta=\Delta$, $\Delta$ being exact) and $F=\lim$, $RF=R\lim$ computed with a K-injective resolution $q_D:D_\bullet\to I_\bullet$, gives a bijection $e:\operatorname{Hom}(X,R\lim D_\bullet)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta X,D_\bullet)$; its characterizing formula with $t=\mathrm{id}$ and a chain map $f:X\to\lim I_\bullet$ gives $e(f)=[q_D]^{-1}\circ(\Delta\lim I_\bullet\to I_\bullet)\circ\Delta f$, and by its functoriality in the first variable $e(\phi)=\epsilon_D\circ\Delta(\phi)$ for every $\phi$, with $\epsilon_D$ the counit normalized in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. In particular $\epsilon_D\circ\Delta(-)$ is injective and $\epsilon$ is natural for strict tower maps. It therefore suffices to compare $\epsilon_D\circ\Delta(-)$ of $\eta_{h,k,N}$ composed with each side. Left side: $\eta_{h,k,N}\circ c^E_{h,k,N}=R\lim(c_{h,k,\bullet})$ by the defining formula, so naturality of $\epsilon$ and Step 3 for $g=kh$ give the tower image $c_{h,k,\bullet}\circ\theta^\Delta_{kh}\circ\Delta(d_{h,k,P})\circ\Delta[h^{-1}k^{-1}(q)]^{-1}$, using $d\circ h^{-1}k^{-1}(q)=(kh)^{-1}(q)\circ d$. Right side: [lem-trf-integral-pullback-resolution-matching] gives $\epsilon_D\circ\Delta(\eta_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^h_M)=u_{h,C_k}\circ h^{-1}(\epsilon_{C_k})$; precomposing with $\Delta h^{-1}(\kappa^k_N)$, using that the exact termwise functor $h^{-1}$ commutes with $\Delta$, and Step 3 for $g=k$ gives $u_{h,C_k}\circ h^{-1}(\theta^\Delta_k)\circ\Delta[h^{-1}k^{-1}(q)]^{-1}$. The two strict tower maps $c_{h,k,m}\circ\theta_{kh,m}\circ d$ and $u_{h,C_{k,m}}\circ h^{-1}(\theta_{k,m})$ from $h^{-1}k^{-1}P$ to $h^*k^*P_m$ both send a local section $x$ to $\bar x\otimes1\otimes1$: the first $\otimes1$ is the $k$-pullback unit and the second the $h$-pullback unit, the termwise compositor being the canonical identification of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] and the computation that of Step 2. Hence the two tower images agree, so by injectivity $\eta_{h,k,N}\circ c^E_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^{kh}_N\circ d_{h,k,N}=\eta_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^h_{Lk^*N}\circ h^{-1}(\kappa^k_N)$, and cancelling the isomorphism $\eta_{h,k,N}$ yields $$c^E_{h,k,N}\circ\kappa^{kh}_N\circ d_{h,k,N}=\kappa^h_{Lk^*N}\circ h^{-1}(\kappa^k_N)$$ in $D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, before any reduction detection.
